title: VelaWorks Onboarding & Ops Huddle

Ravi Shah - Provide initial benchmark script and sampling prompts by 2026-09-20

transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time, I'm Jordan with Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. We'll kick off with quick intros, then run through the onboarding checklist and network requirements. Maya is our CSM and Ravi is our SE.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: Hi all, Lena here, head of MLOps at VelaWorks. Our main goal is a low-latency retrieval assistant for our field apps, and we want to understand hosting options and security posture.
[00:30] Tom Brewer: Tom from platform, we manage their k8s and network boundaries. Quick note: we have strict egress and want to keep data in our VPC where possible.
[00:41] Priya Nair: Priya, security lead. SOC2 type II in progress, also concerned about KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.
[00:49] Jordan Patel: Great, thanks. Couple quick things — typical pattern is start hosted to iterate, then Dedicated or Redwood Priva — sorry private — if you need VPC/HSM. We'll map out options.
[01:05] Ravi Shah: To add, performance-wise we can run a small benchmark. If tail latency under 120–150ms for your 2k token median we can stay hosted, otherwise dedicated or private. I can share a bench script.
[01:22] Chris Young: Quick clarifying question: what's the difference on data retention between hosted and private?
[01:28] Maya Chen: On Hosted, Redwood retains logs for X days by default and you can opt-in to longer logs for audit; with Private your logs stay in your environment and you control retention. We'll send a security pack with exact numbers.
[01:40] Tom Brewer: Is SSO possible for console access? We prefer SAML with our IdP.
[01:45] Jordan Patel: Yes, SAML SSO + RBAC is supported. We'll also walk through SCIM for provisioning if you want.
[01:51] Priya Nair: KMS: we need to integrate our HSM provider for key management, can you support external KMS?
[01:58] Ravi Shah: Yes, Private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption but not direct HSM integration. That's often a gating factor for regulated customers.
[02:10] Lena Ortiz: Timeline— we want a 6-week pilot with production readiness gates. Week one: smoke tests, week two-three: integration, week four-five: load and evals, week six: go/no-go. Is that standard?
[02:22] Maya Chen: Yep that aligns. We'll propose a sprint plan. Also, success metrics we typically capture: 95th percentile latency, token cost per 1k, false positive rate on hallucinations for your retrieval use case.
[02:36] Jordan Patel: Can I ask about current stack—are you using vector DB and what embedding model?
[02:41] Lena Ortiz: We're on Pinecone for vector store, and using an in-house embedding service right now but may migrate.
[02:47] Ravi Shah: Ok, good. We'll need schema of prompt sizes and typical seq lengths — that helps kernel selection and batching recommendations.
[02:56] Tom Brewer: On networking — we must restrict egress and allow only specific Redwood IPs, we use NAT gateways and have private subnets.
[03:05] Jordan Patel: Noted. We can provide a list of egress IPs. For Private we can do VPC peering or private link — depending on your cloud.
[03:15] Priya Nair: About compliance — do you provide audit logs with granular token-level per-user tracing? We need to show who called which model and for what dataset.
[03:25] Maya Chen: Yes, we capture per-request metadata, and in Private deployments logs can be pushed to your SIEM. For Hosted we have encryption at rest and detailed audit trails; exact retention and redaction policies are in the security pack.
[03:40] Chris Young: Any gotchas on cost when switching from Hosted to Dedicated? We have bursty usage.
[03:46] Jordan Patel: Dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved GPUs — cost differentials depend on commit and burst policy. We can model a hybrid routing: host for spikes, dedicated for baseline.
[03:56] Tom Brewer: If bursts are frequent, autoscale could help, but we prefer keeping engineering overhead low.
[04:02] Ravi Shah: Also look at prefix KV caching and batch settings — they'll reduce per-token cost substantially for chatty apps. We'll provide recommended config for your seq length distribution.
[04:12] Lena Ortiz: Cool. Can you talk through the pilot data handling? We will push telemetry and a few customer examples, but everything must be obfuscated.
[04:20] Maya Chen: For evaluations, we support masked data uploads and you can also run bench inside your VPC for Private. We'll sign an NDA for telemetry.
[04:29] Jordan Patel: Alright, going into logistics — next 15 minutes Ravi will walk through the technical checklist and then we do a quick wrap.
[04:38] [screen share noise, brief crosstalk]
[05:10] Ravi Shah: Ok, technical checklist. First: we need 3 sample prompts and a representative long prompt to assess KV size. Second: network allowlist — we'll list endpoints and IP ranges. Third: auth flows — API keys for hosted, mTLS or private endpoint for VPC.
[05:30] Ravi Shah: For the bench script, it'll hit models at a mix of 512 and 2k token contexts to simulate retrieval scenario. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-1k. Expect an initial run to take 2–3 hours depending on sample size.
[05:50] Tom Brewer: That sounds fine. We'll give you NAT IPs and a staging cluster for the private smoke.
[06:00] Priya Nair: On encryption: we require BYOK for keys if private. Is that supported?
[06:05] Ravi Shah: Yes, bring-your-own-key supported for Private deployments. For Hosted we do not accept external HSM but we can do envelope keys and key rotation.
[06:15] Lena Ortiz: Any required contact on Redwood side for compliance questions?
[06:18] Jordan Patel: Priya, you'll work with Maya for SOC2 artifacts and Ravi for technical KMS questions — I'll be the contract owner for pilot pricing.
[06:27] Maya Chen: I'll share a security pack URL in the follow-up chat — it contains SOC2, ISO summaries, pen test dates, and an SSO/SCIM guide.
[06:36] Chris Young: Will you provide a sample runbook for failover — what happens if a model variant is unhealthy?
[06:42] Ravi Shah: Yes, Redwood supports automatic fallback to smaller model variants and region-based failover. We'll share runbook snippets and tracing hooks to connect to your observability.
[06:55] [small interruption: broadband beep]
[07:02] Jordan Patel: Ok, timeline recap: Jordan sends pilot pricing and quota details tomorrow; Ravi shares bench and runbook snippets by Monday; Priya shares SOC2 timelines; Tom to open network ticket. Maya will schedule the 60-min technical bench for 2026-09-23.
[07:18] Priya Nair: One more: we need a formal statement on data residency — can you confirm logs will remain in region us-west-2 for hosted?
[07:25] Maya Chen: I will confirm region residency in the security doc but hosted defaults are region-aware and we'll ensure us-west-2 for this pilot.
[07:35] Lena Ortiz: Great. Anything else we should call out?
[07:40] Chris Young: No, thanks — excited to get started.
[07:44] Jordan Patel: Thanks folks, we'll follow up with the links and invites. End of call.
[07:50] [recording stops]
